scope: Primary literature on docility and prestige, developmental social-learning schedules, evidence conflict and informational cascades, belief rigidity, adviser trust learning, endogenous knowledge, and age-structured demography.
verification_methods: Crossref works API for DOI metadata
PubMed and Europe PMC for biomedical metadata and abstracts
PMC or publisher full text when available
official journal and author-repository copies for access-restricted papers
forward citation tracing from the 13 mandated references

essential_references.title: A Mechanism for Social Selection and Successful Altruism
essential_references.mechanism: Docility is receptivity to social influence that yields gross fitness benefits under bounded rationality while permitting socially induced altruistic costs.
essential_references.main_finding: Selection can sustain costly induced behavior only while the net fitness effect of docility remains positive.
essential_references.model_relevance: Benefits of deference must operate through information or behavior, not a direct reward for deference.
essential_references.limitations: No age structure, empirical calibration, or explicit cultural state dynamics.

essential_references.title: The evolution of prestige: freely conferred deference as a mechanism for enhancing the benefits of cultural transmission
essential_references.mechanism: Learners grant freely conferred deference to successful or knowledgeable models to obtain access; aggregate deference becomes a cue for later model choice.
essential_references.main_finding: Prestige is proposed as an information-goods pathway distinct from coercive dominance.
essential_references.model_relevance: Prestige should be an endogenous and noisy model-quality cue, not identical to adult age or accuracy.
essential_references.limitations: The article's empirical evidence is heterogeneous and does not itself estimate a demographic fitness function.

essential_references.title: A theory of human life history evolution: Diet, intelligence, and longevity
essential_references.journal: Evolutionary Anthropology: Issues, News, and Reviews
essential_references.mechanism: A difficult extractive niche rewards embodied-capital investment in learning and cognition, delayed productivity, intergenerational provisioning, and longevity.
essential_references.main_finding: Extended juvenile dependence and long life are theorized as linked investments that permit acquisition and repayment of productive skills.
essential_references.model_relevance: A direct maturation-to-fecundity bonus is an existing embodied-capital mechanism rather than a new consequence of deference.
essential_references.limitations: The inspected authoritative metadata did not establish a reliable day-level publication date; the theory is not a fitted deference model.

essential_references.title: A Theory of Fads, Fashion, Custom, and Cultural Change as Informational Cascades
essential_references.mechanism: Agents observe previous actions but not private signals; public action imbalance can make ignoring one's private signal optimal.
essential_references.main_finding: Informational cascades create localized conformity and fragile mass behavior because later actions cease to add independent information.
essential_references.model_relevance: Adult agreement must not be treated as independent evidence when adults share a cultural lineage.
essential_references.limitations: No biological demography or developmental stages; final publisher full text was access-restricted in this review.

essential_references.title: Cultural Evolution Develops Its Own Rules: The Rise of Conservatism and Persuasion
essential_references.mechanism: Openness itself is copied, favoring weak susceptibility to others and strong ability to influence others.
essential_references.main_finding: Cultural dynamics can drive rapid conservatism without a genetic conservatism parameter.
essential_references.model_relevance: Adult rigidity can emerge culturally and should not be imposed as a separate genotype.
essential_references.limitations: Simplified pairwise copying and no explicit demographic stage structure.

essential_references.title: Cultural evolution and individual development of openness and conservatism
essential_references.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
essential_references.mechanism: Preferences and propensities governing copying are themselves culturally transmitted during development.
essential_references.main_finding: Cultural dynamics tend toward conservatism; gradual enculturation by many models and larger repertoires can maintain openness.
essential_references.model_relevance: An imposed decline in deference is a special case; evidence-contingent reopening is a more informative comparison.
essential_references.limitations: No two-stage biological demography or rare-mutant invasion in a resource-limited resident environment.

essential_references.title: On optimal learning schedules and the marginal value of cumulative cultural evolution
essential_references.mechanism: Infant, juvenile, and adult stages allocate time between oblique, horizontal, and individual learning while stage lengths coevolve.
essential_references.main_finding: Under cumulative-culture conditions, oblique social learning precedes a juvenile mixture of individual and horizontal learning.
essential_references.model_relevance: Age-varying learning and endogenous learning-stage duration are already established mechanisms.
essential_references.limitations: The model has three learning/life stages and abstract information rather than the exact V4 two-stage demographic system.

essential_references.title: Childhood in social learning models with changing environments: Implications for human evolution
essential_references.mechanism: Observation competes with innovation while childhood imposes a reproductive and resource cost and environments change.
essential_references.main_finding: Stable environments can make costly childhood plus social observation resource-advantageous; sufficiently rapid change reverses the advantage.
essential_references.model_relevance: Environmental, cultural, trust-learning, and maturation timescales must be compared explicitly.
essential_references.limitations: The paper does not estimate a human fitness effect and the publisher final page was access-restricted in this review.

essential_references.title: When does selection favor learning from the old? Social learning in age-structured populations
essential_references.study_type: mathematical age-structured model plus individual-based simulations
essential_references.mechanism: Behavior-dependent survival filters age classes while social-learning strategy and model-age preference evolve.
essential_references.main_finding: Age structure preserves Rogers' paradox; demographic filtering can accumulate adaptation; copy-old is conditional and copy-young can be a compromise.
essential_references.model_relevance: Adult quality must emerge from survival and learning rather than be fixed by source age.
essential_references.limitations: The model is deliberately generic and does not separate public action from private belief.

essential_references.title: Unpredictable benefits of social information can lead to the evolution of individual differences in social learning
essential_references.mechanism: Evolving developmental programmes update social-learning reliance from earlier learning experiences under uncertain social-information value.
essential_references.main_finding: Unpredictability selects flexibility and generates persistent individual differences; low uncertainty favours rigid strategies.
essential_references.model_relevance: The new question cannot be merely fixed versus plastic deference; it must study distinct demographic and cultural feedback.
essential_references.limitations: Does not implement the exact V4 two-stage resource-limited resident-mutant system.

essential_references.title: The coevolution of learning schedules and teaching enhances cumulative knowledge and drives a teacher-innovator syndrome
essential_references.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences
essential_references.study_type: coevolutionary mathematical model plus individual-based simulations
essential_references.mechanism: Vertical, oblique, and individual learning allocation coevolves with parental teaching effort and knowledge-dependent demography.
essential_references.main_finding: Teaching accelerates transfer, frees time for innovation, raises cumulative knowledge, and creates teacher-innovator correlations and sometimes transient producer/scrounger structure.
essential_references.model_relevance: Adult knowledge plus teaching is already an integrated model; V4 requires a distinct erroneous-advice or trust-learning contribution.
essential_references.limitations: The teaching and learning architecture is richer than the minimal V4 system and does not focus on calibrated deference under conflicting evidence.

essential_references.title: The cultural evolution of pluralistic ignorance
essential_references.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
essential_references.mechanism: Public action, private attitude, and second-order belief update on different pathways under material payoff, conformity, dissonance, projection, and cultural tightness.
essential_references.main_finding: Lagged attitude and second-order-belief updating can generate pluralistic ignorance without deception, with different tight- and loose-culture trajectories.
essential_references.model_relevance: Public copying and private belief must be distinct states if V4 discusses conformity, rigidity, or pluralistic ignorance.
essential_references.limitations: No juvenile/adult biological demography or inherited juvenile-deference trait.

essential_references.title: Calibrated deference: Children's evaluations of responses to disagreement across knowledge gaps
essential_references.mechanism: Children evaluate whether deference or persistence is warranted from the relative knowledge and access of the target and corrector, including teachers and peers.
essential_references.main_finding: Children tend to prefer deference to a more knowledgeable source but persistence against an inexpert peer or teacher lacking relevant knowledge; integration is developmentally imperfect.
essential_references.model_relevance: Authority should be a defeasible prior, and private-evidence precision must be able to override it.
essential_references.limitations: Measures third-party evaluations, not participants' own belief updating, heritability, demographic growth, or biological fitness.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Reyes-García V et al. (2008). Do the aged and knowledgeable men enjoy more prestige? Evolution and Human Behavior 29:275-281.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Among 288 Tsimane' men, prestige had only weak association with ethnomedicinal knowledge and no association with age.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Negative evidence against coding adult age as a prestige or expertise proxy.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Behrens TEJ, Hunt LT, Woolrich MW, Rushworth MFS (2008). Associative learning of social value. Nature 456:245-249.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Participants learned both option values and adviser fidelity through dissociable prediction errors and adjusted learning to volatility.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Supports dynamic trust as a learned state rather than fixed advice weight.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Chudek M, Heller S, Birch S, Henrich J (2012). Prestige-biased cultural learning. Evolution and Human Behavior 33:46-56.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Three- and four-year-olds preferentially copied a model who had received bystander attention; transfer was stronger within the demonstrated domain.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Prestige can be a domain-sensitive source prior.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Aoki K, Wakano JY, Lehmann L (2012). Evolutionarily stable learning schedules and cumulative culture in discrete generation models. Theoretical Population Biology 81:300-309.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Formalizes evolutionarily stable ordering and allocation of social and individual learning for cumulative culture.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Establishes age/order-dependent learning as prior art.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Atkisson C, O'Brien MJ, Mesoudi A (2012). Adult Learners in a Novel Environment Use Prestige-Biased Social Learning. Evolutionary Psychology 10:519-537.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Adults in a novel arrowhead-design task used prestige information in model selection, with behaviour changing as direct success information became available.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Prestige cues can be superseded by direct performance evidence.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Diaconescu AO et al. (2014). Inferring on the Intentions of Others by Hierarchical Bayesian Learning. PLOS Computational Biology 10:e1003810.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Models tracking advice accuracy and the volatility of adviser intentions explained choices better than constant-learning-rate alternatives.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Supports fidelity and volatility as separate latent states.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Anderson LR, Holt CA (1997). Information Cascades in the Laboratory. American Economic Review 87:847-862.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Rational cascades formed in most experimental periods in which the public action imbalance made a cascade possible.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Empirical validation that sequential public actions can suppress private signals.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Çelen B, Kariv S (2004). Distinguishing Informational Cascades from Herd Behavior in the Laboratory. American Economic Review 94:484-498.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Belief elicitation distinguishes correlated herd actions from states in which private information no longer affects action.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Observed conformity does not identify a cascade without private-belief information.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Fogarty L, Creanza N, Feldman MW (2019). The life history of learning: Demographic structure changes cultural outcomes. PLOS Computational Biology 15:e1006821.
forward_primary_studies.finding: A combined demographic and cultural framework shows that learning life histories can change cultural trajectories and demographic outcomes.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Age structure plus culture is established prior art.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Rollwage M, Dolan RJ, Fleming SM (2018). Metacognitive Failure as a Feature of Those Holding Radical Beliefs. Current Biology 28:4014-4021.e8.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Radical belief endorsement was associated with poorer metacognitive insight and smaller confidence shifts after disconfirming evidence in a perceptual task.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Rigidity can operate through confidence and evidence weighting rather than a fixed deference trait.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Anglin SM (2019). Do beliefs yield to evidence? Journal of Experimental Social Psychology 82:176-199.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Across four studies, participants generally moved with empirical evidence even when it challenged prior views, although evidence-quality judgments could be biased.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Negative evidence against assuming universal belief perseverance or backfire.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Wood T, Porter E (2019). The Elusive Backfire Effect: Mass Attitudes' Steadfast Factual Adherence. Political Behavior 41:135-163.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Across correction experiments, factual backfire was difficult to elicit as a general response.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: V4 should include correction and reopening rather than hard-code entrenchment.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Kappes A et al. (2020). Confirmation bias in the utilization of others' opinion strength. Nature Neuroscience 23:130-137.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Participants underused the strength of disconfirming opinions while using the strength of confirming opinions, with reduced neural sensitivity to disconfirming strength.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Provides an evidence-asymmetry mechanism for rigidity.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Deffner D, McElreath R (2020). The importance of life history and population regulation for the evolution of social learning. Philosophical Transactions B 375:20190492.
forward_primary_studies.finding: The adaptive value and evolution of social learning depend on life history and how populations are regulated.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Demographic growth and evolutionary selection cannot be inferred from an unregulated learning payoff alone.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Diaconescu AO et al. (2020). Neural arbitration between social and individual learning systems. eLife 9:e54051.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Relative precision in hierarchical learning models captured behavioral and neural arbitration between social and individual information.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Supports explicit precision-weighting rather than unconditional copying.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Hertz U, Bell V, Raihani N (2021). Trusting and learning from others. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 288:20211414.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Advice produced stronger immediate following than observed choices, moderated by trust; long-run model fits separated sustained social reliance from reversion to trial-and-error.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Immediate deference and learned persistent reliance are distinct.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Ammar M, Fogarty L, Kandler A (2023). Social learning and memory. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 120:e2310033120.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Memory architecture changes the informational value and evolutionary consequences of social learning.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: A persistent cultural or trust state is not innocuous and requires an explicit forgetting rule.

forward_primary_studies.citation: Pereg M, Hertz U, Ben-Artzi I, Shahar N (2024). Disentangling the contribution of individual and social learning processes in human advice-taking behavior. npj Science of Learning 9:4.
forward_primary_studies.finding: Repeated advice had a strong causal effect and models separated informed advice-taking from a stable baseline bias to follow advice.
forward_primary_studies.relevance: Motivates separate inherited prior/bias and learned fidelity states.

ranked_gaps.gap: Age/stage demography coupled to learned adviser fidelity under explicit private-social evidence conflict and resident-generated adult culture.
ranked_gaps.reason: No traced primary study combined all of these elements; absence remains provisional.

ranked_gaps.gap: Identifying private belief revision separately from public conformity and prestige-guided source choice.
ranked_gaps.reason: Primary cascade, prestige, and pluralistic-ignorance models explicitly show different latent mechanisms can generate similar actions.

ranked_gaps.gap: Independence-aware social evidence across generations with shared cultural and source-specific error.
ranked_gaps.reason: Cascade theory establishes the problem, but the broader literature was not exhaustively enumerated.

ranked_gaps.gap: Developmental reopening after early enculturation when adviser fidelity reverses before versus after maturation.
ranked_gaps.reason: The openness and volatility-aware trust literatures provide complementary but usually separate mechanisms.

ranked_gaps.gap: Longitudinal empirical calibration linking childhood deference and adult cultural competence to survival and reproduction.
ranked_gaps.reason: The scoped empirical studies measure decisions, confidence, evaluations, or task rewards rather than biological fitness.
